name: Classifyber - segmentation
summary: Segments white matter bundles from a whole-brain tractogram with Classifyber, a pre-trained streamline-based linear classifier, after ANTs registration to MNI152; outputs a WMC classification and per-bundle .tck files.
description: Runs only the test phase of Classifyber: the tractogram is registered to the MNI152 T1 template via an ANTs warp computed from the subject T1, then pre-trained classifiers segment the bundles selected by ID (HCP-IFOF, HCP-minor, HCP-major and clinical sets listed in the README) and the result is converted to multiple .tck files. The tractogram and T1 must be in the same space. Classifiers are tuned to tractograms of a given size (for example about 500K streamlines for HCP-minor), so results may be poor otherwise. Use brainlife.app.228 to train on your own examples. This branch runs with Python 3.

parameters.description: ID list of the bundles of interest, separated by commas, e.g. 32, 40, 45  (refer to the README.md for the mapping)
parameters.placeholder: allowed values: from 21 to 30, from 32 to 33, from 35 to 36, and from 38 to 45

citations.text: Berto G et al. Classifyber, a robust streamline-based linear classifier for white matter bundle segmentation. NeuroImage (2020).
Avesani P et al. The open diffusion data derivatives, brain data upcycling via integrated publishing of derivatives and reproducible open cloud services. Sci Data 6:69 (2019).

failure_modes.fix: Check that the selected tract IDs produced streamlines.
